claim: Strain VYD135α was generated by using the CRISPR-Cas9 system targeting centromeric transposons in the lab strain H99α.
source: In a previous study, we generated a genome-shuffled strain of C. neoformans, VYD135α, by using the CRISPR-Cas9 system targeting centromeric transposons in the lab strain H99α.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the method used to generate VYD135α, referencing a previous study.

claim: Strain VYD135α exhibits multiple centromere-mediated chromosome arm exchanges compared to the parental strain H99α.
source: This led to multiple centromere-mediated chromosome arm exchanges in strain VYD135α when compared to the parental strain H99α, without any detectable changes in gene content between the two genomes (Yadav et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the genomic changes in VYD135α and cites a previous publication.

claim: Strain VYD135α exhibits severe sporulation defects when mated with strain KN99a.
source: In addition, strain VYD135α exhibits severe sporulation defects when mated with strain KN99a (which is congenic with strain H99α but has the opposite mating type), likely due to the extensive chromosomal rearrangements introduced into the VYD135α strain.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the sporulation phenotype observed in crosses.

claim: The genome-shuffled strain VYD135α can produce spores in crosses with MATa C. neoformans strains after prolonged incubation.
source: In this study, we show that the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α can in fact produce spores in crosses with MATa C. neoformans strains after prolonged incubation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding as a key result of the study.

claim: Products from each individual basidium in VYD135α crosses contain genetic material derived from only one of the two parents.
source: Analysis of these spores reveals that the products from each individual basidium contain genetic material derived from only one of the two parents.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding based on spore analysis.

claim: Whole-genome sequencing of the progeny revealed an absence of recombination between the two parental genomes.
source: Whole-genome sequencing of the progeny revealed an absence of recombination between the two parental genomes.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The mitochondria in progeny from VYD135α crosses were found to always be inherited from the MATa parent.
source: The mitochondria in these progeny were found to always be inherited from the MATa parent, consistent with known mitochondrial uniparental inheritance (UPI) patterns in C. neoformans (Sun et al., 2020a).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the mitochondrial inheritance pattern and cites supporting literature.

claim: Only one of the parental nuclei was present in the terminal sporulating basidium in some instances.
source: Analysis of strains expressing fluorescent reporter proteins revealed instances where only one of the parental nuclei was present in the terminal sporulating basidium.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Pseudosexual reproduction was detected in natural isolate crosses.
source: We also observed the occurrence of such uniparental nuclear inheritance in wild-type and natural isolate crosses.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from crosses with natural isolates.

claim: Pseudosexual reproduction in natural isolate crosses resulted in mainly MATα progeny.
source: Pseudosexual reproduction was also detected in natural isolate crosses where it resulted in mainly MATα progeny, a bias observed in Cryptococcus ecological distribution as well.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and connects it to ecological patterns.

claim: The meiotic recombinase Dmc1 was found to be critical for pseudosexual reproduction.
source: The meiotic recombinase Dmc1 was found to be critical for pseudosexual reproduction.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from genetic analysis.

claim: Co-incubation of strain KN99a with strain VYD135α resulted in hyphal development and basidia production, but no spores were observed during a standard 2-week incubation.
source: Co-incubation of the wild-type strain KN99a with the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α resulted in hyphal development and basidia production, but no spores were observed during a standard 2-week incubation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the mating phenotype observed.

claim: A limited number of sporulating basidia (16/1201=1.3%) were observed in the VYD135α×KN99a cross after 5 weeks.
source: However, when sporulation was assessed at later time points in the VYD135α×KN99a cross, we observed a limited number of sporulating basidia (16/1201=1.3%) after 5 weeks compared to a much greater level of sporulation in the wild-type H99α×KN99a cross (524/599=88%) (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references figures showing the phenotype.

claim: The wild-type H99α×KN99a cross showed 88% sporulation frequency (524/599) after 5 weeks.
source: However, when sporulation was assessed at later time points in the VYD135α×KN99a cross, we observed a limited number of sporulating basidia (16/1201=1.3%) after 5 weeks compared to a much greater level of sporulation in the wild-type H99α×KN99a cross (524/599=88%) (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references figures.

claim: None of the strains H99α, KN99a, and VYD135α exhibited any filamentation on their own even after 5 weeks of incubation.
source: None of these strains exhibited any filamentation on their own even after 5 weeks of incubation, indicating that the sporulation events were not a result of unisexual reproduction (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references supporting figures.

claim: The sporulation events in VYD135α×KN99a crosses were not a result of unisexual reproduction.
source: None of these strains exhibited any filamentation on their own even after 5 weeks of incubation, indicating that the sporulation events were not a result of unisexual reproduction (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the lack of self-filamentation.

claim: Genotyping of the H99α×KN99a progeny revealed that both MATa and MATα progeny were produced from each basidium.
source: As expected, genotyping of the mating-type locus in the H99α×KN99a progeny revealed that both MATa and MATα progeny were produced from each basidium (Figure 1E and G, Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references supporting data.

claim: All germinating progeny from individual basidia in the VYD135α×KN99a cross possessed either only the MATα or the MATa allele.
source: In contrast, the same analysis for VYD135α×KN99a revealed that all germinating progeny from each individual basidium possessed either only the MATα or the MATa allele (Figure 1E and G, Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references supporting data.

claim: The mitochondria in all progeny from VYD135α×KN99a crosses were inherited from the MATa parent.
source: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays also revealed that the mitochondria in all of these progeny were inherited from the MATa parent, in accord with known UPI (Figure 1F–G).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from PCR analysis.

claim: The presence of mitochondria from only the MATa parent in MATα progeny confirmed that these progeny were the products of fusion between the parent strains.
source: The presence of mitochondria from only the MATa parent in MATα progeny further confirmed that these progeny were the products of fusion between the parent strains and were not the products of unisexual reproduction.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on mitochondrial inheritance patterns.

claim: In the wild-type H99α×KN99a cross, most basidia formed robust spore chains with both fluorescent colors observed in them.
source: In the wild-type cross, most of the basidia formed robust spore chains with both fluorescent colors observed in them, while a small population (~1%) of basidia exhibited spore chains with only one color, representing uniparental nuclear inheritance (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Approximately 1% of basidia in the wild-type H99α×KN99a cross exhibited spore chains with only one fluorescent color, representing uniparental nuclear inheritance.
source: In the wild-type cross, most of the basidia formed robust spore chains with both fluorescent colors observed in them, while a small population (~1%) of basidia exhibited spore chains with only one color, representing uniparental nuclear inheritance (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The majority of the basidium population in the VYD135α×KN99a cross did not exhibit sporulation, and the two parental nuclei appeared fused but undivided.
source: In contrast, the majority of the basidium population in the shuffled-strain VYD135α×KN99a cross did not exhibit sporulation, and the two parental nuclei appeared fused but undivided (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: A few basidia (~1%) in the VYD135α×KN99a cross bore spore chains with only one fluorescent color, marking uniparental nuclear inheritance events.
source: A few basidia (~1%) bore spore chains with only one fluorescent color, marking uniparental nuclear inheritance events.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The uniparental basidia accounted for all of the sporulating basidia in the VYD135α×KN99a cross.
source: While the basidia with uniparental nuclear inheritance in the H99α×KN99a cross were a small fraction (~1%) of sporulating basidia, the uniparental basidia accounted for all of the sporulating basidia in the VYD135α×KN99a cross.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding comparing the two crosses.

claim: Uniparental nuclear inheritance leads to the generation of clonal progeny but requires mating and cell-cell fusion between parents of two opposite mating types.
source: Taken together, these results show that the uniparental nuclear inheritance leads to the generation of clonal progeny but requires mating, the cell-cell fusion between parents of two opposite mating types.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: The process of uniparental nuclear inheritance during sporulation in C. neoformans is defined as pseudosexual reproduction.
source: Based on these observations, we define the process of uniparental nuclear inheritance during sporulation in C. neoformans as pseudosexual reproduction (and it is referred to as such hereafter).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly defines this new term for the observed phenomenon.

claim: H99α and Bt63a exhibit approximately 0.5% genetic divergence.
source: As mentioned previously, H99α (as well as the H99α-derived strain VYD135α) and Bt63a have approximately 0.5% genetic divergence.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the genetic divergence between these strains.

claim: IUM96a belongs to the same lineage as H99α/KN99a (VNI) and exhibits approximately 0.1% genome divergence from the H99α reference genome.
source: IUM96a belongs to the same lineage as H99α/KN99a (VNI) and exhibits approximately 0.1% genome divergence from the H99α reference genome.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the lineage and genetic divergence of IUM96a.

claim: Bt63a belongs to a different lineage of the C. neoformans species (VNBI) and exhibits ~0.5% genetic divergence from the H99α/KN99a genome.
source: Bt63a belongs to a different lineage of the C. neoformans species (VNBI) and exhibits ~0.5% genetic divergence from the H99α/KN99a genome.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the lineage and genetic divergence of Bt63a.

claim: Both Bt63a and IUM96a genomes exhibit one reciprocal chromosome translocation with H99α.
source: Both the Bt63a and the IUM96a genomes exhibit one reciprocal chromosome translocation with H99α, and as a result, share a total of 10 chromosome-level changes with the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this genomic feature and references a figure.

claim: Bt63a and IUM96a share a total of 10 chromosome-level changes with the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α.
source: Both the Bt63a and the IUM96a genomes exhibit one reciprocal chromosome translocation with H99α, and as a result, share a total of 10 chromosome-level changes with the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this genomic comparison and references a figure.

claim: Neither Bt63a nor IUM96a are self-filamentous even after prolonged incubation on mating media.
source: None of these strains are self-filamentous even after prolonged incubation on mating media but both cross efficiently with H99α and VYD135α (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references a figure.

claim: Both Bt63a and IUM96a cross efficiently with H99α and VYD135α.
source: None of these strains are self-filamentous even after prolonged incubation on mating media but both cross efficiently with H99α and VYD135α (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references a figure.

claim: The H99α×Bt63a strains crossed rapidly (within a week) producing robust sporulation from most of the basidia observed.
source: The H99α×Bt63a strains crossed rapidly (within a week) producing robust sporulation from most of the basidia observed.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the mating phenotype.

claim: The VYD135α×Bt63a cross underwent a low frequency of sporulation (12 spore-producing basidia/840 basidia=1.4%) in 2–3 weeks.
source: The VYD135α×Bt63a cross underwent a low frequency of sporulation (12 spore-producing basidia/840 basidia=1.4%) in 2–3 weeks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references a figure.

claim: Dissection of spores from the H99α×Bt63a cross revealed a low germination frequency (average of 25%).
source: Dissection of spores from the H99α×Bt63a cross revealed a low germination frequency (average of 25%) with two of the basidia showing no spore germination at all (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references supplementary data.

claim: Almost 75% of the meiotic events in the H99α×Bt63a cross generated progeny that were heterozygous for the MAT locus.
source: Genotyping of germinated spores from the H99α×Bt63a cross revealed both MATa and MATα progeny from individual basidia, with almost 75% of the meiotic events generating progeny that were heterozygous for the MAT locus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references figures and supplementary data.

claim: Spores from 15/20 basidia in the VYD135α×Bt63a cross germinated and displayed a higher germination frequency than the H99α×Bt63a cross.
source: For the VYD135α×Bt63a cross, spores from 15/20 basidia germinated and displayed a higher germination frequency than the H99α×Bt63a cross (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references supplementary data.

claim: All germinated progeny from the VYD135α×Bt63a cross harbored only the MATα mating type.
source: Interestingly, all germinated progeny harbored only the MATα mating type, whereas the mitochondria were in all cases inherited from the MATa parent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: The mitochondria in all progeny from the VYD135α×Bt63a cross were inherited from the MATa parent.
source: Interestingly, all germinated progeny harbored only the MATα mating type, whereas the mitochondria were in all cases inherited from the MATa parent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references a figure.

claim: Crosses with strain IUM96a revealed a low level of sporulation (19/842=2.3%) with VYD135α.
source: Crosses with strain IUM96a also revealed a low level of sporulation (19/842=2.3%) with VYD135α but a high sporulation frequency with H99α (91%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references a figure.

claim: Crosses with strain IUM96a revealed a high sporulation frequency with H99α (91%).
source: Crosses with strain IUM96a also revealed a low level of sporulation (19/842=2.3%) with VYD135α but a high sporulation frequency with H99α (91%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references a figure.

claim: The progeny from H99α×IUM96a exhibited variable basidium-specific germination frequencies and inherited both MATa and MATα in each basidium.
source: Analysis of progeny from crosses involving IUM96a revealed a similar pattern to what was observed with crosses involving KN99a. The progeny from H99α×IUM96a exhibited variable basidium-specific germination frequencies and inherited both MATa and MATα in each basidium, whereas VYD135α×IUM96a progeny from each basidium inherited exclusively either MATa or MATα (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this finding and references figures and supplementary data.

claim: VYD135α×IUM96a progeny from each basidium inherited exclusively either MATa or MATα.
source: Analysis of progeny from crosses involving IUM96a revealed a similar pattern to what was observed with crosses involving KN99a. The progeny from H99α×IUM96a exhibited variable basidium-specific germination frequencies and inherited both MATa and MATα in each basidium, whereas VYD135α×IUM96a progeny from each basidium inherited exclusively either MATa or MATα (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this finding and references figures and supplementary data.

claim: Co-incident uniparental MAT inheritance and a high germination frequency were observed in progeny of basidia 7, 8, and 9 from the H99α×IUM96a cross.
source: Interestingly, we observed co-incident uniparental MAT inheritance and a high germination frequency in progeny of basidia 7, 8, and 9 from the H99α×IUM96a cross as well (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation and references figures and supplementary data.

claim: Pseudosexual reproduction occurs in nature in parallel with canonical sexual reproduction.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that this unusual mode of sexual reproduction occurs with multiple natural isolates. We further propose that pseudosexual reproduction occurs in nature in parallel with canonical sexual reproduction.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly proposes this based on the findings with natural isolates.

claim: For the H99α×Bt63a cross, both parents contributed to the nuclear composition of their progeny.
source: As expected, for the H99α×Bt63a cross, both parents contributed to the nuclear composition of their progeny, and there was clear evidence of meiotic recombination as determined by variant analysis (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: There was clear evidence of meiotic recombination in the H99α×Bt63a progeny as determined by variant analysis.
source: As expected, for the H99α×Bt63a cross, both parents contributed to the nuclear composition of their progeny, and there was clear evidence of meiotic recombination as determined by variant analysis (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The nuclear genome in each of the VYD135α×Bt63a progeny was found to be inherited exclusively from only the VYD135α parent.
source: However, when the VYD135α×Bt63a progeny were similarly analyzed, the nuclear genome in each of the progeny was found to be inherited exclusively from only the VYD135α parent (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3), and the progeny exhibited sequence differences across the entire Bt63a genome.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The VYD135α×Bt63a progeny exhibited sequence differences across the entire Bt63a genome.
source: However, when the VYD135α×Bt63a progeny were similarly analyzed, the nuclear genome in each of the progeny was found to be inherited exclusively from only the VYD135α parent (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 3), and the progeny exhibited sequence differences across the entire Bt63a genome.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The mitochondrial genome in VYD135α×Bt63a progeny was inherited exclusively from the Bt63a parent.
source: In contrast, the mitochondrial genome was inherited exclusively from the Bt63a parent (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 4), in accord with the PCR assay results discussed above.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: Most of the H99α×Bt63a progeny exhibited aneuploidy.
source: In addition, the whole-genome sequencing data also revealed that while most of the H99α×Bt63a progeny exhibited aneuploidy, the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α×Bt63a progeny were euploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A and B), and based on flow cytometry analysis, these uniparental progeny were haploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The genome-shuffled strain VYD135α×Bt63a progeny were euploid.
source: In addition, the whole-genome sequencing data also revealed that while most of the H99α×Bt63a progeny exhibited aneuploidy, the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α×Bt63a progeny were euploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A and B), and based on flow cytometry analysis, these uniparental progeny were haploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: Based on flow cytometry analysis, the VYD135α×Bt63a uniparental progeny were haploid.
source: In addition, the whole-genome sequencing data also revealed that while most of the H99α×Bt63a progeny exhibited aneuploidy, the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α×Bt63a progeny were euploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A and B), and based on flow cytometry analysis, these uniparental progeny were haploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from flow cytometry analysis.

claim: The H99α×IUM96a progeny exhibited signs of meiotic recombination.
source: The progeny from crosses involving IUM96a as the MATa partner were also sequenced. Similar to the Bt63a analysis, the H99α×IUM96a progeny exhibited signs of meiotic recombination, whereas the VYD135α ×IUM96a progeny did not (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The VYD135α×IUM96a progeny did not exhibit signs of meiotic recombination.
source: The progeny from crosses involving IUM96a as the MATa partner were also sequenced. Similar to the Bt63a analysis, the H99α×IUM96a progeny exhibited signs of meiotic recombination, whereas the VYD135α ×IUM96a progeny did not (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The progeny in each of the basidia from VYD135α×IUM96a crosses exclusively inherited nuclear genetic material from only one of the two parents.
source: Congruent with the mating-type analysis, the progeny in each of the basidia exclusively inherited nuclear genetic material from only one of the two parents.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The H99α×IUM96a progeny were found to be aneuploid for some chromosomes.
source: Furthermore, the H99α×IUM96a progeny were found to be aneuploid for some chromosomes, while the VYD135α×IUM96a progeny were completely euploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 7).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The VYD135α×IUM96a progeny were completely euploid.
source: Furthermore, the H99α×IUM96a progeny were found to be aneuploid for some chromosomes, while the VYD135α×IUM96a progeny were completely euploid (Figure 3—figure supplement 7).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: Four progeny from basidium 7 from the H99α×IUM96a cross harbored only H99α nuclear DNA and had no contribution from the IUM96a nuclear genome.
source: We also sequenced four progeny from basidium 7 from the H99α×IUM96a cross, which were suspected to be uniparental progeny based on mating-type PCRs. This analysis showed that all four progeny harbored only H99α nuclear DNA and had no contribution from the IUM96a nuclear genome, further supporting the conclusion that pseudosexual reproduction occurs in wild-type crosses (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: The mitochondria in progeny from basidium 7 of the H99α×IUM96a cross were inherited from the MATa parent.
source: Similar to other progeny, the mitochondria in these progeny were inherited from the MATa parent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding.

claim: Genome exclusion in C. neoformans occurs during mitotic hyphal growth and not during meiosis.
source: Using fluorescence microscopy, we examined the steps of nuclear exclusion in C. neoformans and found that it occurs during mitotic hyphal growth and not during meiosis.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from fluorescence microscopy analysis.

claim: Genome exclusion could happen with either of the two parents in C. neoformans.
source: We also observed that genome exclusion could happen with either of the two parents in C. neoformans, similar to what has also been reported for water frogs.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and compares it to findings in other organisms.

claim: Imaging of long hyphae in the wild-type cross revealed the presence of pairs of nuclei with both fluorescent markers along the length of the majority of hyphae.
source: As expected, imaging of long hyphae in the wild-type cross revealed the presence of pairs of nuclei with both fluorescent markers along the length of the majority of hyphae (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Tracking of hyphae from basidia with spore chains in the VYD135α×KN99a cross revealed hyphal branches with only one parental nucleus, which were preceded by a hyphum with both parental nuclei.
source: In contrast, tracking of hyphae from basidia with spore chains in the genome-shuffled strain VYD135α×KN99a cross revealed hyphal branches with only one parental nucleus, which were preceded by a hyphum with both parental nuclei (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Seven events of nuclear loss at hyphal branching were observed in independent experiments.
source: In total, we observed seven events of nuclear loss at hyphal branching in independent experiments and were able to track two of them to observe sporulation or basidia formation at the tip.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data from microscopy observations.

claim: Long hyphae with only one parental nucleus were observed in the VYD135α×Bt63a cross.
source: We also observed long hyphae with only one parental nucleus in the VYD135α×Bt63a cross as well, suggesting the mechanism might be similar between strains.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes this observation from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Hyphal branching may facilitate the separation of one parental nucleus from the main hyphae harboring both parental nuclei.
source: These results suggest that hyphal branching may facilitate the separation of one parental nucleus from the main hyphae harboring both parental nuclei.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly proposes this mechanism based on microscopy observations.

claim: A previous report documented that dmc1Δ bilateral crosses display significantly reduced, but not completely abolished, sporulation in Cryptococcus.
source: A previous report documented that dmc1Δ bilateral crosses (both the parents are mutant for DMC1) display significantly reduced, but not completely abolished, sporulation in Cryptococcus (Lin et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous publication for this finding.

claim: A small percentage (21/760=2.7%) of basidia in the H99α dmc1Δ×KN99a dmc1Δ cross bypassed the requirement for Dmc1 and produced spores.
source: We observed a similar phenotype with the H99α dmc1Δ×KN99a dmc1Δ cross. While most of the basidia were devoid of spore chains, a small percentage (21/760=2.7%) of the population bypassed the requirement for Dmc1 and produced spores (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references figures.

claim: The germination frequency for spores from the H99α dmc1Δ×KN99a dmc1Δ cross was found to be very low (~22% on average).
source: When dissected, the germination frequency for these spores was found to be very low (~22% on average) with spores from many basidia not germinating at all (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references supplementary data.

claim: Many fewer basidia (~0.1%) in the VYD135α dmc1Δ×KN99a dmc1Δ cross produced spore chains as compared to ~1% sporulation in VYD135α×KN99a.
source: For VYD135α dmc1Δ×KN99a dmc1Δ, many fewer basidia (~0.1%) produced spore chains as compared to ~1% sporulation in VYD135α×KN99a (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references figures.

claim: dmc1 mutant unilateral crosses sporulated at a frequency of 0.4%.
source: dmc1 mutant unilateral crosses (one of the two parents is mutant and the other one is wild-type) sporulated at a frequency of 0.4% suggesting that only one of the parental strains was producing spores (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references a figure.

claim: The DMC1 deletion led to a 20-fold reduction in viable sporulation in the VYD135α×KN99a cross.
source: Overall, the DMC1 deletion led to a 20-fold reduction in viable sporulation in the VYD135α×KN99a cross, observed as a ten fold decrease from the number of sporulation events in the bilateral cross and a further two fold reduction in the number of basidia producing viable spores.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: All 11 observed basidia with only the GFP-H4 fluorescence signal (VYD135α nuclei) were found to produce spores in the VYD135α×KN99a dmc1Δ cross.
source: Indeed, all 11 observed basidia with only the GFP-H4 fluorescence signal were found to produce spores, but only 2 out of 19 mCherry-H4 containing basidia exhibited sporulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references a figure.

claim: Only 2 out of 19 mCherry-H4 containing basidia (KN99a dmc1Δ nuclei) exhibited sporulation in the VYD135α×KN99a dmc1Δ cross.
source: Indeed, all 11 observed basidia with only the GFP-H4 fluorescence signal were found to produce spores, but only 2 out of 19 mCherry-H4 containing basidia exhibited sporulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific quantitative data and references a figure.

claim: Dmc1 is critical for pseudosexual reproduction.
source: These results combined with the spore dissection findings show that Dmc1 is critical for pseudosexual reproduction.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the genetic analysis.

claim: Most (>95%) of Cryptococcus natural isolates belong to only one mating type, α.
source: Most (>95%) of Cryptococcus natural isolates belong to only one mating type, α (Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this ecological observation and cites a reference.

claim: Endoreplication is known to occur in the sister species C. deneoformans during unisexual reproduction.
source: Endoreplication is known to occur in the sister species C. deneoformans during unisexual reproduction, and we think that this is the most likely route via which ploidy is increased during pseudosexual reproduction.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this known fact and proposes its relevance to pseudosexual reproduction.

claim: Hybridogenesis has only been observed in the animal kingdom in some species of frogs, fishes, and snakes.
source: Currently, hybridogenesis has only been observed in the animal kingdom in some species of frogs, fishes, and snakes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the current knowledge about hybridogenesis distribution.

claim: Plants exhibit parthenogenesis (aka apomixis), along with gynogenesis and androgenesis.
